question: Should Workboard retain direct operator acceptance as a valid transition to `done`, or should all existing and future completions require the proposed structured-proof policy?
rationale: The linked issue explicitly leaves this policy unresolved, while current documentation establishes manual acceptance as supported behavior; selecting a global fail-closed rule would deliberately change existing user workflows and persisted-card compatibility.

options.title: Preserve accepted manual completion
options.body: Keep direct operator acceptance compatible and apply stricter proof checks only to automated completion paths or a separately designed verification state.

options.title: Adopt strict completion globally
options.body: Approve the new policy only with explicit updated documentation, a narrow migration or recovery path for existing cards, and fresh-install plus upgrade proof.

options.title: Pause pending Workboard policy design
options.body: Close or defer this implementation until maintainers settle the completion-state and authority model in the linked proposal.

recommendation.title: Preserve accepted manual completion
recommendation.body: Keep direct operator acceptance compatible and apply stricter proof checks only to automated completion paths or a separately designed verification state.

likelyOwner.reason: They authored the linked proposal and can provide the intended policy rationale, though a repository owner should make the final product decision.
